records.old_rule: Design contract §3 and ruling 8.3a: search by construct with the v2 two-route strategy E AND (I OR O); the post-exercise/recovery T-block is diagnostic only; the 0-72 h window and all eligibility rules are applied at screening
records.new_rule: The post-exercise/acute-bout T-block is a required concept: E AND (I OR O) AND T. T does not encode the 0-72 h organising window, which with all eligibility rules is still applied at screening; open-window-type terms remain OR supplements or citation-chasing routes only. PRESS accepted with conditions: no infection-outcome terms in the strategy (eligibility via the immune-link rule; infection outcomes charted when present); train* retained until the pilot sample test; protocol E no longer claims the strategy covers infection terms
records.reason: PubMed validation showed the construct-at-screening strategy is not screenable by two reviewers (255,019 records, about 8,500 person-hours of title/abstract screening before the other four databases), whereas requiring T reduced volume to about 15,900 records with 10/10 positive PubMed seeds retrieved. Trade-off disclosed as recall versus feasibility. Mitigations: positive seed set expanded to >=30 (including >=5 numeric-only timing reports) and re-tested in the pilot; backward/forward citation chasing of included studies and the five citation-chasing reviews (Peake 2017, Campbell & Turner 2018, Simpson 2020, Shi 2025, Xie 2026); T-free sensitivity run on a random sample during the pilot

records.old_rule: Protocol v3.0 section G and 05_extraction v3.0: measurements row = "one assay-level tested-universe summary OR one named candidate/feature x comparison", enumerating all named immune candidates in accessible article text AND supplements; sample_sets row = one group x assay/platform x matrix x exact time, split when n or process differs; precision_validation = one row per report/cohort/measurement x domain; no time-bin boundary rule ("unknown timing is not imputed to a bin"); no denominator rule for several reported n; no background disposition (EXCLUDE_TA/EXCLUDE_FT mapped to "excluded, or background if retained for context") and background charting depth left to the manual; figure values digitised under a predeclared two-reviewer procedure when needed; adult status by reported age without an operational rule (unreported age = awaiting classification); legacy matrix/exercise_mode/training_status/design/time_unit entered as free text
records.new_rule: Row units: measurements = one named analyte x one author-reported test (conventional/targeted); omics = one assay_universe_summary row per analysis universe + every candidate named in the main text, main tables or figure legends, candidates prespecified in aims/methods always enumerated, supplementary result tables summarised by counts and locators, set-level results one reported_result_summary row per analysis; sample_sets = one row per cohort x group/arm x matrix x time point as sampled, platforms in assay_platform, split by platform only when a platform-specific n is reported and differs, subgroups only when subgroup n and results are reported; precision_validation = seven domain rows per report x cohort x marker family (new optional last column precision_validation.marker_family), analyte-level rows only for analyte-specific evidence, measurement_id single ID or null; mandatory ID patterns. Vocabulary: marker_family + mucosal_antimicrobial_protein (conventional; analytes classified by analyte, not platform); sample_role + periodic_training_monitoring, resting_habitual_group (nonexercise_control vs matched_control defined); candidate_selection_rule + statistically_selected_hits_from_untargeted_screen; candidate_selection_basis + results_statistical_selection; record_type and candidate_* fields defined (candidate_* apply to all non-universe rows; prespecification refers to the named candidate; result_status follows the author-reported test and threshold); controlled lists for matrix, exercise_mode, training_status, design, time_unit (field names unchanged); screening disposition RETAIN_BACKGROUND (administrative full-text status, not a scientific exclusion, no primary FT code, maps to scope_stream background). Time bins: value = earliest stated bound; straddling interval -> later bin + TIME_BIN_STRADDLE; day-level timing -> nominal hours + DAY_LEVEL_TIMING; "immediately after" without a number -> 0_to_lt30min + IMMEDIATE_NONNUMERIC; bin IDs, order and window positions unchanged. Denominators: n_recruited = pre-exclusion enrolment; n_analyzed = analysed n for the primary immune outcome, other denominators in notes; per-platform n only when reported; counts integer or missing code only; DERIVED_N for arithmetic derivations. Missing-value decision tree (NA by row type/design, NR not reported, UNCLEAR conflicting) and no-inference rule. Age rule: adult when an explicit range/minimum >= 18 y is reported or mean - 2*SD >= 18 y; otherwise AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION (not FT03) unless the report states < 18 y participants. Background reports (scope_stream background): bibliographic, design, population, platforms and n only, no per-marker results, no precision_validation rows, one extractor + one checker. Figure-only values are not digitised: direction and significance only, effect_value NR, figure_panel_locator filled, flag FIGURE_ONLY. Also: author_window_interpretation coded from the authors' own voice, exhaustive, one locator per value; immune_link exhaustive, omics_integration at analysis level; one reports row per version (reference_id suffix, version stubs DUPLICATE_VERSION / scope NA, linked to the study family after verification); publication_status = review/version status only, short-format article type in version_label, version_date ISO 8601 (online > issue > accepted with flag); screening/consensus fields copy-only in charting workbooks

records.old_rule: Protocol v3.0 section F and 04_screening v3.0: one title/abstract stage. Two reviewers independently screen the title and abstract of every deduplicated record (ADVANCE / EXCLUDE_TA with one FT01-FT08 code / AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION / FRONTIER_PREPRINT), calibrated by the 50-record title/abstract pilot (raw agreement >= 80% on the binary disposition and all conceptual disagreements resolved); conflicts discussed and, if unresolved, adjudicated.
records.new_rule: Two-stage screening. Stage 1 (TITLE, TI): two reviewers independently screen every deduplicated record seeing only title, source/journal, year, document type, DOI and PMID, with no abstract and no AI hint. Dispositions ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT, EXCLUDE_TITLE (one code from a closed list of title-evident reasons: TI01 review/editorial/protocol/conference abstract evident from title or document type -> FT01; TI02 animal or in-vitro only -> FT02; TI03 cohort clearly < 18 y -> FT03; TI04 no exercise or physical-activity context evident -> FT04; TI05 no immune, inflammatory or omics content evident -> FT07) and AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION; anything else is ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT. Consensus is automatic: any ADVANCE wins, EXCLUDE_TITLE only when both reviewers chose it; conflicts are logged, not adjudicated. Calibration: a 100-record title pilot sampled from the deduplicated formal union (seed 20261005) must reach raw agreement >= 80% on the binary TI disposition before formal stage 1. Abstract completion (between stages): abstracts for the stage-1 retained set are taken, in order, from (1) database exports that contain them (PubMed, Web of Science full record), (2) PubMed by PMID or DOI->PMID (NCBI ID Converter), (3) the source database full record (Scopus COMPLETE view where entitled; Embase/SPORTDiscus exports), (4) a manual request list for A (fulltext_requests/abstract_requests.csv); a record with no obtainable abstract is screened at stage 2 on title and available text and marked abstract_unavailable, never excluded for that reason. Stage 2 (TITLE/ABSTRACT, TA): v3 rules unchanged (ADVANCE / EXCLUDE_TA with FT code / AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION / FRONTIER_PREPRINT), dual independent, no AI hints, conflicts discussed and adjudicated; a 25-record re-calibration under v3.1 (seed 20261003, from the stage-1 retained set) precedes formal stage 2. The PRISMA-ScR flow gains a stage-1 box; counts are reported per stage and stage-1 exclusions by closed-list code.
records.reason: Feasibility with protected recall. The five-database raw volume is estimated at 60,000-90,000 records (PubMed 20,090; Web of Science EO route 6,669; Scopus EO route 6,159 on 2026-10-05), and abstracts are not uniformly available through database APIs off campus. Title screening is about 3-4 times faster than title/abstract screening. Recall is protected by the narrow closed list of title-evident reasons and the advance-wins rule; all other eligibility judgements move to stage 2 or full text.

editorial_choices_for_confirmation: TI04 and TI05 require positive evidence in the title (a non-exercise exposure, or named outcomes none of which is immune/inflammatory/omics); a title that names no exposure or no outcome advances.
TI03 applies only to cohorts that the title shows to be entirely < 18 y; youth, junior, young or student cohorts and mixed adolescent/adult cohorts advance.
AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION paired with EXCLUDE_TITLE (or both AWAITING) yields AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION, which proceeds to abstract completion and stage 2 like ADVANCE_TO_ABSTRACT.
Two EXCLUDE_TITLE decisions with different codes keep the earlier code in closed-list order; the difference is logged.
Title-pilot pass rule is raw agreement only (no concept-resolution condition); repeat rounds use seed 20261005 + round_number - 1.
TA re-calibration is round 2 of the TA calibration: seed 20261003 by the existing repeat-seed rule, 25 records from the stage-1 retained set.
Stage 1 and stage 2 use separate workbooks: stage-1 records_master holds no abstracts; stage-2 records_master holds only the stage-1 retained set with completed abstracts.

records.title: Database set, search-stage limits and strategy v0.9
records.old_rule: Protocol v3.0/v3.1 (PRE-003) section E, design contract §3, 8.3a and §9: five databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Embase, SPORTDiscus); two routes E AND (I OR O) AND T (immune route EI and omics route EO, exported separately and deduplicated); all eligibility rules applied at screening rather than in the query (no species, age, publication-type or language limits); strategy v0.7 (immun* truncation, bare run and (physical AND activit*) in the E block, generic exercise words in title/abstract, bare complement and cytotoxic* anywhere, T block including time course, time-course, pre and post, baseline and post); Web of Science Topic and Scopus TITLE-ABS-KEY fields; PRESS sign-off by A on 2026-10-04 (v0.7)
records.new_rule: (1) Database set: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, plus Google Scholar as a documented supplementary search (not a core database). Embase and SPORTDiscus are withdrawn (licence/feasibility; D exports manually from the web interfaces; API routes abandoned). (2) Search-stage limits: (a) PubMed animal-only exclusion NOT (animals[mh] NOT humans[mh]) (Cochrane/CADTH form; keeps unindexed records); (b) publication-type exclusion of reviews, editorials, letters, comments and case reports in PubMed, and document-type exclusion in Web of Science (Review, Editorial Material, Letter, Correction) and Scopus (re, ed, le, no, er, sh, cr); (c) PubMed child-only exclusion NOT ((infant[mh] OR child[mh] OR adolescent[mh]) NOT adult[mh]) (keeps mixed-age and unindexed records). These move part of FT02 (animal-only), FT01 (source type) and FT03 (children only) into the query; FT01-FT08 and their hierarchy are unchanged at screening. Reviews removed by (b) are kept as a logged, non-screened citation-chasing source list. Web of Science and Scopus have no species or age tag, so FT02/FT03 remain screening rules there. (3) Strategy v0.9: generic exercise words (e.g. sport*, train*, competition*, race*, endurance, aerobic) in titles only; bare run and the loose (physical AND activit*) pair removed; immun* replaced by a semantic immune list (immunoassay/immunoblot/immunofluorescence method words no longer count as immune concepts); bare complement and cytotoxic* restricted to titles, with specific phrases in abstracts; T loses time course, time-course, pre and post, baseline and post and gains the Package B recall terms (preexercise, postrace, prerace, hr/hrs after/post, h/min/hours of recovery, acute effects, marathon*, ultramarathon*, triathlon*, ironman); single route E AND I AND T (omics route E AND O AND T dropped; omics vocabulary kept for charting/tagging); Web of Science and Scopus searched in title, abstract and author-keyword fields rather than Topic / TITLE-ABS-KEY, conditional on D's 10-seed test, with fallback to the broad fields. (4) Google Scholar supplement: short strings (256-character limit, no truncation) recorded verbatim; first 200 results per string sorted by relevance; date, number screened and stopping rule logged; records enter the same two-stage screening; reported under PRISMA-S as a supplementary source. (5) A's PRESS sign-off of 2026-10-04 (v0.7) is void; A re-reviews v0.9 before the formal search Addendum (A, 2026-10-05, after D's first Web of Science and Scopus runs): the core routes are also limited to English-language records and journal articles in all three databases (PubMed AND english[la] NOT preprint[pt], preprints staying in the supplementary preprint search; Web of Science DT=(Article) AND LA=(English); Scopus DOCTYPE(ar OR ip) AND LANGUAGE(english)). Non-English reports and non-article formats are lost at search and this is disclosed as a limitation; citation chasing, Google Scholar and the preprint supplement are not language-limited.
records.reason: Feasibility and precision with recall checked on seeds. The v0.7 five-database projection (about 33,000-48,000 unique records; 03_search/strategy_review_2026-10-05.md) was 2-3 times the largest published benchmark and could not be screened by two reviewers; Embase and SPORTDiscus were withdrawn for licence and feasibility reasons (manual web-interface export by D; API routes abandoned). Benchmark of 23 published reviews: identified-records median 2,360; broad/scoping subgroup median 4,690, maximum 10,976. PubMed diagnostics (2026-10-05, not formal searches): v0.7 union 20,090; v0.8 (animal NOT + generic-E title-only + publication-type NOT) 11,448; plus the child-only NOT, removal of run and (physical AND activit*), the semantic immune list and the title restriction of complement and cytotoxic* 9,577; plus removal of four generic T phrases 8,909; single route E AND I AND T 7,733; plus Package B (+280) 8,013 (2026-10-05T13:03:39Z, query SHA-256 prefix e30ec141aac4); plus English-language limit and NOT preprint[pt] 7,846 (final v0.9, 2026-10-05T13:23:01Z, prefix 6ad15420fe1f; the preprint seed POS-S3 drops out by design). Projected unique volume roughly 9,000-13,000 records. The omics route is redundant for eligible studies: under the immune-link rule an eligible omics study has an identifiable immune anchor, so E AND O AND I AND T is a subset of E AND I AND T, and none of 61 positive seeds was retrieved only by the omics route. Trade-off disclosed: Embase adds unique records in biomedical reviews (Bramer et al. 2017: MEDLINE + Embase + Web of Science + Google Scholar needed for about 98% recall; reference to be added) and SPORTDiscus indexes sport-science journals not all covered by Scopus/Web of Science. Mitigations: citation chasing of all included reports and of the five open-window reviews, the Google Scholar supplement and the expanded seed set

records.title: AI-stand-in first-pass screening with mandatory human verification (stages 1 and 2)
records.old_rule: Protocol v3.1 (PRE-005) section F and screening manual sections 3A/3B: two HUMAN reviewers independently screen every deduplicated record at each stage with no AI involvement ("AI does not make automatic exclusions, replace either reviewer or show reviewers any hint at any stage"); conflicts are discussed between the two human reviewers and adjudicated if unresolved; calibration is by human pilots only (100-record title pilot, 25-record stage-2 re-calibration).
records.new_rule: AI-assisted screening with mandatory human verification, replacing the no-AI sentence of section F. (1) First pass: two AI stand-in screeners with different prompt orientations (B side: inclusion-oriented, default ADVANCE, exclude only on a clearly established reason; C side: closed-list-strict; both read every record individually, keyword classifiers forbidden) independently screen every record of a stage; each writes per-batch JSON decisions (disposition, FT/TI code, study-type hint, short note), archived under 04_screening/formal_2026-10-05_v0.9/ai_stage1/ and ai_stage2/. (2) PRE-005 merge rules unchanged (any ADVANCE wins; conflict = disposition difference or, for agreed exclusions, code difference). (3) Every record on which the two stand-ins disagree receives a blind third AI read, recorded separately. (4) Human verification (decisions of record; by B and C independently in their workbooks): ALL AI-advanced records (full-text candidates), every conflict without a third read, every AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION record, and a seeded 10% random sample of agreed AI exclusions with AI columns hidden (seed 20261005); an ADVANCE found inside the sample triggers re-screening of that record type. (5) Agreed AI exclusions outside the sample are listed and reported separately in the PRISMA-ScR flow as AI exclusions with 10% sample verification, per stage and code. (6) Reviewer workbooks show the AI columns except in the sample-verification sheet. (7) The 100-record random title-pilot sample (seed 20261005) is issued to B and C as a blind calibration set with AI columns hidden; the AI-versus-human comparison on it is the reported stand-in reliability check. (8) The manuscript discloses the design and models in Methods and Acknowledgments; 01_protocol/ai_use_log.json records the runs.
records.reason: Feasibility at the actual deduplicated volume (15,750 records; ~44 h per person for dual human title screening alone, before stage 2), with recall protected by the advance-wins merge, the closed exclusion lists, third reads of every disagreement and mandatory human verification of all advances plus a seeded 10% exclusion sample. A decided on 2026-10-05 to adopt the design and start screening immediately without waiting for amendment text, with formal disclosure deferred to the manuscript; PRE-007 registers that decision retrospectively on 2026-10-06 at A's instruction in the recovery session.

records.title: Validation-readiness triage of stage-2 advances with AI element extraction, GPT-6 Sol adjudication and layered human verification
records.old_rule: PRE-007 item 4, applied at stage 2: "Human verification (decisions of record; by B and C independently in their workbooks): ALL AI-advanced records (full-text candidates), every conflict without a third read, every AWAITING_CLASSIFICATION record, and a seeded 10% random sample of agreed AI exclusions with AI columns hidden (seed 20261005)"; and protocol v3.1 section F: "the human reviewers later screen **all** sought full texts". Under these rules all 4,326 stage-2 AI advances would be verified by B and C and sought at full text.
records.new_rule: (1) Triage population: the stage-2 AI advances (4,298 when the triage was built; the 28 later batch-235 advances are triaged the same way before human verification). (2) First pass: two model families independently extract five abstract-level elements with verbatim quotes and no eligibility decision, under prompt v1.1 (ai_triage/prompt_v1.md): E1 exercise exposure, E2 post-exercise sampling, E3 immune marker, E4 population, E5 validation-readiness element; GLM-5.3-Flash (thinking off) and GPT-6 Luna (reasoning effort max). (3) Adjudication: records on which the families disagree (1,532) and records in the validation layer only through repeated_monitoring (459) receive a blind read by GPT-6 Sol (reasoning effort medium) under prompt v1.2 (ai_triage/prompt_e5_adjudication_v1_2.md; stricter E5); Sol's elements are final for those records, first-pass agreed elements for the rest. (4) Layers from the final elements: X = a core element absent (E1 no exercise exposure; E2 no post-exercise sample; E3 no immune marker; E4 under 18, clinical/infected or non-human); V = core present and E5 present under the v1.2 operational definition (protocol C: metric_validation; outcome_linkage with a measured infection/URTI/illness/overtraining/performance outcome analysed against the marker; omics_discovery; repeated_monitoring across >=3 bouts or a season/training block with monitoring purpose, crossover/randomised condition comparisons excluded); M = core present, E5 absent; U = E5 unclear or no valid output. (5) Human verification by B and C independently, D adjudicating: all V records (E5 and E4 confirmed per record, AI quotes visible; E1-E3 judged at full text); all U records (decide the layer); a seeded 10% sample within M and within X (seed 20261005); a seeded 10% sample of Sol-adjudicated records (seed 20261008), overriding the layer scope. A V record found in the M sample, or a record with all core elements found in the X sample, triggers a re-check of that pattern across the layer. (6) Only confirmed V records proceed to full-text retrieval, full-text screening (FT01-FT08 unchanged) and data extraction. M is charted from title/abstract elements only, without full text, and is shown as a separate box in the PRISMA-ScR flow. X is treated as AI exclusion at title/abstract level with the seeded 10% sample, on the same footing as the stage-2 AI exclusions of PRE-007. (7) This layered scope replaces PRE-007's stage-2 verification of all advances; stage-1 verification (seeded 10% exclusion sample and the 100-record blind title pilot) and the stage-2 10% sample of agreed exclusions are unchanged. (8) Methods report the three models and settings, prompt versions v1.1 and v1.2, the two-family agreement statistics and Sol-versus-family agreement; the post-hoc narrowing of the full-text scope is listed as a limitation.
records.reason: Feasibility and focus. The stage-2 AI pass left 4,326 full-text candidates, beyond what B and C can verify and read at full text, while the review's deliverable (the per-marker validation-readiness map) depends on records that carry a validation element. The triage concentrates full-text work on those records and keeps the rest visible as an abstract-level evidence map rather than discarding them. A spot check of first-pass outputs on 2026-10-08 found E5 over-called (crossover designs counted as repeated monitoring; background framing counted as outcome linkage; remarks on individual differences counted as metric validation), which led to the stricter v1.2 definition and the GPT-6 Sol adjudication of disagreements and repeated_monitoring-only V records.
records.work_stage: after stage-2 AI screening (completed 2026-10-07: 9,277 screened, 4,326 ADVANCE, 4,949 EXCLUDE_TA, 2 AWAITING) and before any human verification of stage 2, full-text retrieval or extraction; first-pass triage runs 2026-10-07/08, adjudication 2026-10-08
records.information_already_known: Stage-1 and stage-2 AI outputs, the two-family first-pass elements and the GPT-6 Sol adjudication, including the layer counts (V 577, M 3,020, X 697, U 4), were known when A adopted the decisions. No full text had been read and no human verification of stage 2 had started. Because the full-text scope was narrowed after these counts were known, the narrowing is post hoc and is reported as a limitation.
records.decision_by: A (2026-10-08; six editorial choices adopted, each with the recommended option; see editorial_choices)

editorial_choices.adopted_option: Only the validation-readiness layer (V) proceeds to full-text screening and data extraction; the evidence-map layer (M) is charted from title/abstract elements only (no full text) and shown as a separate box in the PRISMA-ScR flow

The v1.2 validation-readiness element definition with four sub-types: metric_validation; outcome_linkage with a measured infection/URTI/illness/overtraining/performance outcome analysed against the marker; omics_discovery; repeated_monitoring across >=3 bouts or a season/training block with monitoring purpose (crossover/randomised condition comparisons do not count)

Core element absent at abstract level (no exercise exposure, no post-exercise sample, no immune marker, or population under 18, clinical or non-human) is treated as AI exclusion at title/abstract level with a seeded 10% human sample, on the same footing as the stage-2 AI exclusions of PRE-007
B and C confirm E5 (validation element) and E4 (population) per record with the AI quotes visible; E1-E3 are judged at full text
PRE-007 and PRE-008 bundled into protocol release v3.2 (GitHub tag and Zenodo version DOI under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23147972) before human verification and full-text screening start

Methods report the three models (GLM-5.3-Flash thinking off, first pass; GPT-6 Luna reasoning effort max, first pass; GPT-6 Sol reasoning effort medium, adjudication), prompt versions (v1.1 first pass; v1.2 adjudication), two-family agreement statistics and Sol-versus-family agreement; the post-hoc narrowing of the full-text scope is listed as a limitation
